issue.title: [202511][Regression][snappi] PFCWD does not drop packets on congestion after changing from PFCWD forward mode to PFCWD drop mode.

failure.body:
### Is it platform specific

broadcom

### Importance or Severity

High

### Description of the bug

Following testcase was executed: tests/snappi_tests/pfcwd/test_pfcwd_actions.py

The test-script has following sub-testcases.
test_pfcwd_frwd_90_10
test_pfcwd_drop_over_subs_40_09

In the first test, the PFCWD is configured in the forward mode.

In the 2nd testcase, the PFCWD is set to default (drop mode).

In the 2nd testcase, it has 2 ingress and 1 egress port and is sending 49% traffic on each ingress. Hence there is no congestion on ingress side. However, egress is receiving PFCs and hence lossless traffic would be dropped on the egress side.

It is seen that although the PFCWD config shows that PFCWD is in "drop" mode, packets are passed to the egress and to IXIA without dropping any packets. Hence testcase fails.

The PFCWD stats show that egress port is in 'stormed' mode but does not drop any packets.

On further investigation, it was seen that no ACL is applied on egress and hence no drops on egress for the lossless traffic.

Since this is not a production scenario, marking the issue as 'high'. Marking this as regression as this works fine in 202405. Workaround is to stop PFCWD before moving to 'drop' mode.

@saksarav-nokia @rawal01

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure the PFCWD in forward mode on ingress port.
```
        sudo pfcwd stop
        sudo pfcwd start --action forward 200 --restoration-time 200
```

2. Check the PFCWD configuration.
3. Move the PFCWD to default mode.
```
sudo pfcwd start_default
```
4. Check the PFCWD configuration and ensure that it is in DROP mode.
5. Start the traffic on ingress and ensure that egress receives PFC and is in stormed mode.
6. Check for dropped packets on the egress.

### Actual Behavior and Expected Behavior

If the PFCWD is in 'drop' mode, then PFC storm (for lossless priorities) is received on egress, it should drop lossless packets.
